significance: The Loudun possessions (1632-1634) — collective alleged demonic possession of Ursuline nuns, directed against the priest Urbain Grandier — combined sexual scandal, political intrigue, and demonological doctrine in one of early modern Europe's most sensational cases. Grandier was tortured and burned in 1634; the possessions themselves became a theater of exorcism that drew audiences from across France. Michel de Certeau's analysis in The Possession at Loudun (1970) is the most sustained scholarly treatment.
source_method: Contemporary published accounts; analyzed in de Certeau, The Possession at Loudun (1970/2000); Hutton, The Witch (2017)
